children.text: Chapter 1
athāto dīkṣāṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, we shall explain <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).

children.text: bhagavān paramaśivabhaṭṭārakaḥ śrutyādyaṣṭādaśavidyāḥ sarvāṇi darśanāni līlayā tattadavasthāpannaḥ praṇīya saṃvinmayyā bhagavatyā bhairavyā svātmābhinnayā pṛṣṭaḥ pañcabhiḥ mukhaiḥ pañcāmnāyān paramārthasārabhūtān praṇināya ||
children.translated_text: The blessed venerable supreme <s>Śiva</s>, having playfully assumed the states of all the eighteen branches of knowledge beginning with revelation and all systems of doctrine, composed, when asked by the blessed <s>Bhairavī</s>, who is made of consciousness and non-different from his own self, the five transmissions from his five mouths, which are the essence of ultimate truth.

children.text: tatrāyaṃ siddhāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here this is the doctrine.

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśattattvāni viśvam ||
children.translated_text: The thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles) are the universe.

children.text: śarīrakañcukitaḥ śivo jīvo niṣkañcukaḥ paraśivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, enclosed in the sheath of the body, is the individual soul; without sheaths he is <s>Paraśiva</s>.

children.text: svavimarśaḥ puruṣārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One's own reflective awareness is the human goal.

children.text: varṇātmakā nityāḥ śabdāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sounds, whose nature is phonemic, are eternal.

children.text: mantrāṇām acintyaśaktitā ||
children.translated_text: Mantras possess inconceivable power.

children.text: saṃpradāyaviśvāsābhyāṃ sarvasiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: All accomplishment comes through tradition and faith.

children.text: viśvāsabhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāmāṇyam ||
children.translated_text: Authority rests chiefly on faith.

children.text: aikyaniṣphālanād antarātmavittiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the breaking open of unity there is knowledge of the inner self.

children.text: ānandaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ tac ca dehe vyavasthitaṃ tasyābhivyañjakāḥ pañca makārāḥ tair arcanaṃ guptyā prākaṭyān nirayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bliss is the form of <s>Brahman</s>, and it is situated in the body; the five makāras are its manifesters. Worship is to be performed with them in secrecy; from making them public comes hell.

children.text: bhāvanādārḍhyād ājñāsiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through firmness of contemplative realization there is success in command.

children.text: sarvadarśanānindā ||
children.translated_text: There is no disparagement of any system of doctrine.

children.text: agaṇanaṃ kasyāpi ||
children.translated_text: There is no reckoning of anyone.

children.text: sacchiṣye rahasyakathanam ||
children.translated_text: Secret teaching is to be spoken to a true disciple.

children.text: sadā vidyānusaṃhatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There should always be continuity of the <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: satataṃ śivatāsamāveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There should be constant immersion in the state of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: kāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryāvihitahiṃsāsteyalokavidviṣṭavarjanam ||
children.translated_text: One must avoid lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy, forbidden violence, theft, and what is hated by people.

children.text: ekagurūpāstir asaṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Service to one guru alone is free from doubt.

children.text: sarvatra niṣparigrahatā ||
children.translated_text: Everywhere there should be absence of possessiveness.

children.text: phalaṃ tyaktvā karmakaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Action should be performed after abandoning its fruit.

children.text: anityakarmalopaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Occasional rites may be omitted.

children.text: mapañcakālābhe 'pi nityakramapratyavamṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even when the five makāras are unavailable, there should be reflective recollection of the regular sequence.

children.text: nirbhayatā sarvatra ||
children.translated_text: There should be fearlessness everywhere.

children.text: sarvaṃ vedyaṃ havyam indriyāṇi srucaḥ śaktayo jvālāḥ svātmā śivaḥ pāvakaḥ svayam eva hotā ||
children.translated_text: Everything knowable is the oblation; the senses are the ladles; the powers are the flames; one's own self, <s>Śiva</s>, is the fire; one oneself is the sacrificer.

children.text: nirviṣayacidvimṛṣṭiḥ phalam ||
children.translated_text: Reflection on consciousness without objects is the fruit.

children.text: ātmalābhān na paraṃ vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Nothing is higher than the attainment of the self.

children.text: saiṣā śāstraśailī ||
children.translated_text: This is the manner of the scripture.

children.text: veśyā iva prakaṭā vedādividyāḥ
children.translated_text: The branches of knowledge beginning with the Veda are public, like courtesans.

children.text: sarveṣu darśaneṣu gupteyaṃ vidyā ||
children.translated_text: Among all systems of doctrine this <s>vidyā</s> is secret.

children.text: tatra sarvathā matimān dīkṣeta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, by all means, an intelligent person should undergo initiation.

children.text: dīkṣās tisraḥ śāktī śāmbhavī māntrī ceti
children.translated_text: Initiations are three: <s>śāktī</s>, <s>śāmbhavī</s>, and <s>māntrī</s>.

children.text: māntrī mantropadiṣṭayā sarvāś ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māntrī</s> is performed through instruction in mantra; and one may perform all of them.

children.text: ekaikāṃ vety eke ||
children.translated_text: Some say that each may be performed separately.

children.text: sadguruḥ kramaṃ pravartya sāṅgaṃ hutvā taruṇollāsavān śiṣyam āhūya vāsasā mukhaṃ baddhvā gaṇapatilalitāśyāmāvārtālīparāpātrabindubhis tam avokṣya siddhāntaṃ śrāvayitvā ||
children.translated_text: The true guru, having set the sequence in motion and having offered the complete oblation, should call the disciple, who is possessed of youthful exhilaration, bind his face with a cloth, sprinkle him with drops from the vessels of <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Vārtālī</s>, and <s>Parā</s>, and make him hear the doctrine.

children.text: tacchirasi raktaśuklacaraṇaṃ bhāvayitvā tadamṛtakṣālitaṃ sarvaśarīram alaṃkuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having visualized red and white feet on his head, he should adorn the disciple's whole body as washed by their nectar.

children.text: tasyāmūlam ā brahmabilaṃ prajvalantīṃ prakāśalaharīṃ jvaladanalanibhāṃ dhyātvā tadraśmibhis tasya pāpapāśān dagdhvā ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on a blazing wave of light, like flaming fire, extending from his root up to the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>, he should burn away the disciple's sins and bonds with its rays.

children.text: trikaṭutriphalācaturjātatakkolamadayantīsahadevīdūrvābhasmamṛttikācandanakuṅkumarocanākarpūravāsitajalapūrṇaṃ vastrayugaveṣṭitaṃ nūtanakalaśaṃ bālāṣaḍaṅgenābhyarcya śrīśyāmāvārtālīcakrāṇi nikṣipya tisṛṇām āvaraṇamantrair abhyarcya saṃrakṣyāstreṇa pradarśya dhenuyonī ||
children.translated_text: He should worship with the six limbs of <s>Bālā</s> a new jar wrapped in a pair of cloths and filled with water scented with the three pungents, the three myrobalans, the four aromatics, takkolā, madayantī, sahadevī, dūrvā grass, ash, earth, sandal, saffron, yellow pigment, and camphor; he should place in it the cakras of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, and <s>Vārtālī</s>, worship them with the enclosure mantras of the three goddesses, protect it with the weapon mantra, and display the cow and womb gestures.

children.text: śivayuksauvarṇakarṇike svaradvandvajuṣṭakiñjalkāṣṭake kacaṭatapayaśalākṣaravargāṣṭayuktāṣṭadale digaṣṭakasthita ṭhaṃ vaṃ caturaśre mātṛkāyantre śiṣyaṃ niveśya tena kumbhāmbhasā tisṛbhiḥ vidyābhiḥ snapayet ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>mātṛkāyantra</s>, whose golden pericarp is joined with <s>Śiva</s>, whose eight filaments are occupied by the pairs of vowels, whose eight petals contain the eight groups of letters beginning with ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, śa, and la, whose eight directions are established, and whose square contains ṭhaṃ and vaṃ, he should seat the disciple and bathe him with that jar-water by means of the three <s>vidyās</s>.

children.text: sadukūlaṃ sālepaṃ sābharaṇaṃ samālaṃ suprasannaṃ śiṣyaṃ pārśve niveśya mātṛkāṃ tadaṅge vinyasya vimuktamukhakarpaṭasya tasya haste trīn prathamasiktān candanokṣitān dvitīyakhaṇḍān puṣpakhaṇḍān nikṣipya tattvamantrair grāsayitvā dakṣiṇakarṇe bālam upadiśya paścād iṣṭamanuṃ vadet ||
children.translated_text: He should seat beside him the disciple, dressed in fine cloth, anointed, ornamented, garlanded, and very pleased; having installed the <s>mātṛkā</s> on his limbs, and after removing the cloth from his face, he should place in his hand three first-moistened pieces anointed with sandal and three flower-pieces, make him eat them with the <s>tattva</s> mantras, teach <s>Bālā</s> into his right ear, and afterward speak the desired mantra.

children.text: tatas tasya śirasi svacaraṇaṃ nikṣipya sarvān mantrān sakṛd vā krameṇa vā yathādhikāram upadiśya svāṅgeṣu kimapy aṅgaṃ śiṣyaṃ sparśayitvā tadaṅgamātṛkāvarṇādi dvyakṣaraṃ tryakṣaraṃ caturakṣaraṃ vā ānandanāthaśabdāntaṃ tasya nāma diśet ||
children.translated_text: Then, placing his own foot on the disciple's head, he should teach all the mantras, either once or in sequence, according to eligibility; having caused the disciple to touch some limb on his own body, he should give him a name made from the <s>mātṛkā</s> syllable or other letter of that limb, of two, three, or four syllables, ending in the word <s>Ānandanātha</s>.

children.text: bālopadiṣṭeḥ pūrvam ātmanaḥ pādukāṃ ṣaṭtārayuktāṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Before the instruction in <s>Bālā</s>, he should give his own sandals joined with the six <s>tāras</s>.

children.text: ācārān anuśiṣya hārdacaitanyam āmṛśya vidyātrayeṇa tadaṅgaṃ triḥ parimṛjya parirabhya mūrdhany avaghrāya svātmarūpaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having instructed him in the modes of conduct, having touched the consciousness in the heart, having wiped his body three times with the three <s>vidyās</s>, embraced him, and smelled his head, he should make him of the nature of his own self.

children.text: śiṣyo 'pi pūrṇatāṃ bhāvayitvā kṛtārthas taṃ guruṃ yathāśakti vittair upacarya viditaveditavyo 'śeṣamantrādhikārī bhaved iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: The disciple too, having contemplated fullness, having achieved his aim, and having honored that guru with wealth according to his ability, should become one who knows what is to be known and who has authority over all mantras. Thus auspiciousness.

children.text: Chapter 2
itthaṃ sadguror āhitadīkṣaḥ mahāvidyārādhanapratyūhāpohāya gāṇanāyakīṃ paddhatim āmṛśet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having received initiation from a true guru, one should take up the method of <s>Gāṇanāyakī</s> in order to remove obstacles to the worship of the great <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: brāhme muhūrta utthāya dvādaśānte sahasradalakamalakarṇikāmadhyaniviṣṭagurucaraṇayugalavigaladamṛtarasavisarapariplutākhilāṅgo hṛdayakamalamadhye jvalantam udyadaruṇakoṭipāṭalam aśeṣadoṣanirveṣabhūtam anekapānanaṃ niyamitapavanamanogatir dhyātvā tatprabhāpaṭalapāṭalīkṛtatanuḥ bahir nirgatya muktamalamūtro dantadhāvanasnānavastraparidhānasūryārghyadānāni vidhāya udyadādityavartine mahāgaṇapataye tatpuruṣāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi ||
children.translated_text: Having risen in the brāhma muhūrta, he should meditate on his entire body as flooded by the spreading stream of nectar dripping from the pair of feet of the guru, who is established in the middle of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus at the dvādaśānta; and, within the lotus of the heart, on the one who blazes, red like ten million rising suns, who is the expiation of all faults, who has many lotus-faces, and whose movement of breath and mind is restrained. His own body made red by the expanse of that radiance, he should go outside, pass feces and urine, clean his teeth, bathe, put on garments, and give the sun-offering. To <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, abiding in the rising sun: 'We know that <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; we meditate on the one with the curved trunk.'

children.text: āyur ārogyam aiśvaryaṃ balaṃ puṣṭir mahadyaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Long life, health, sovereignty, strength, nourishment, and great fame,

children.text: kavitvaṃ bhuktimuktī ca caturāvṛttitarpaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: poetic power, enjoyment, and liberation arise from the fourfold round of satiation-offerings.

children.text: prathamaṃ dvādaśavāraṃ mūlamantreṇa tarpayitvā mantrāṣṭāviṃśativarṇān svāhāntān ekaikaṃ caturvāraṃ mūlaṃ ca caturvāraṃ tarpayitvā punaḥ śrīśrīpatigirijāgirijāpatiratiratipatimahīmahīpatimahālakṣmīmahālakṣmīpatiṛddhyāmodasamṛddhipramodakāntisumukhamadanāvatīdurmukhamadadravāvighnadrāviṇīvighnakartṛvasudhārāśaṅkhanidhivasumatīpadmanidhitrayodaśamithuneṣv ekaikāṃ devatāṃ caturvāraṃ mūlaṃ caturvāraṃ ca tarpayet evaṃ catuścatvāriṃśadadhikacatuśśatatarpaṇāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: First, having satiated him twelve times with the root mantra, he should satiate each of the twenty-eight syllables of the mantra, ending in svāhā, four times each, and the root mantra four times. Then, among the thirteen pairs, <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Śrīpati</s>, <s>Girijā</s> and <s>Girijāpati</s>, <s>Rati</s> and <s>Ratipati</s>, <s>Mahī</s> and <s>Mahīpati</s>, <s>Mahālakṣmī</s> and <s>Mahālakṣmīpati</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>Āmoda</s>, <s>Samṛddhi</s> and <s>Pramoda</s>, <s>Kānti</s> and <s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Madanāvatī</s> and <s>Durmukha</s>, <s>Madadravā</s> and <s>Vighnadrāviṇī</s>, <s>Vighnakartṛ</s> and <s>Vasudhārā</s>, <s>Śaṅkhanidhi</s> and <s>Vasumatī</s>, <s>Padmanidhi</s>, he should satiate each deity four times and the root mantra four times. Thus there are four hundred and forty-four satiation-offerings.

children.text: atha yāgavidhiḥ gṛham āgatya sthaṇḍilam upalipya dvāradeśa ubhayapārśvayor bhadrakālyai bhairavāya dvārordhve lambodarāya namaḥ iti antaḥpraviśya āsanamantreṇa āsane sthitvā prāṇān āyamya ṣaḍaṅgāni vinyasya mūlena vyāpakaṃ kṛtvā svātmani devaṃ siddhalakṣmīsamāśliṣṭapārśvam ardhenduśekharam āraktavarṇaṃ mātuluṅgagadāpuṇḍrekṣukārmukaśūlasudarśanaśaṅkhapāśotpaladhānyamañjarīnijadantāñcalaratnakalaśapariṣkṛtapāṇyekādaśakaṃ prabhinnakaṭam ānandapūrṇam aśeṣavighnadhvaṃsanighnaṃ vighneśvaraṃ dhyātvā ||
children.translated_text: Now the rite of sacrifice: having come home, smeared the altar-ground, and said 'Obeisance to <s>Bhadrakālī</s>' and 'to <s>Bhairava</s>' on the two sides of the doorway, and 'Obeisance to <s>Lambodara</s>' above the doorway, he should enter within. Seated on the seat by means of the seat-mantra, he should restrain the breaths, install the six limbs, make the pervasive installation with the root mantra, and meditate within himself on the deity <s>Vighneśvara</s>: embraced at his side by <s>Siddhalakṣmī</s>, bearing the crescent moon as crest, red in color, with eleven hands adorned with citron, mace, sugarcane bow, trident, discus, conch, noose, blue lotus, cluster of grain, the tip of his own tusk, and a jeweled water-pot, with temples split open, full of bliss, intent on destroying all obstacles.

children.text: purato mūlasaptābhimantritena gandhākṣatapuṣpapūjitena śuddhena vāriṇā trikoṇaṣaṭkoṇavṛttacaturaśrāṇi vidhāya tasmin puṣpāṇi vikīrya vahnīśāsuravāyuṣu madhye dikṣu ca ṣaḍaṅgāni vinyasya agnimaṇḍalāya daśakalātmane arghyapātrādhārāya namaḥ sūryamaṇḍalāya dvādaśakalātmane arghyapātrāya namaḥ somamaṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśakalātmane arghyāmṛtāya namaḥ iti śuddhajalam āpūrya astreṇa saṃrakṣya kavacenāvakuṇṭhya dhenuyonimudrāṃ pradarśayet ||
children.translated_text: In front, with pure water that has been consecrated seven times with the root mantra and worshiped with sandal, unhusked rice, and flowers, he should form a triangle, hexagon, circle, and square. Having scattered flowers there and installed the six limbs in the directions of fire, lord, demon, and wind, in the middle, and in the intermediate directions, he should say: 'Obeisance to the fire maṇḍala, consisting of ten kalās, the support of the arghya vessel; obeisance to the sun maṇḍala, consisting of twelve kalās, the arghya vessel; obeisance to the moon maṇḍala, consisting of sixteen kalās, the nectar of the arghya.' Having filled it with pure water, protected it with the weapon-mantra, enclosed it with the armor-mantra, he should display the cow-womb mudrā.

children.text: saptavāram abhimantrya tajjalavipruḍbhir ātmānaṃ pūjopakaraṇāni ca saṃprokṣya tajjalena pūrvoktaṃ maṇḍalaṃ parikalpya tadvad ādimaṃ saṃyojya tatropādimaṃ madhyamaṃ ca nikṣipya vahnyarkendukalāḥ abhyarcya vakratuṇḍagāyatryā gaṇānāṃ tvety anayā ṛcā cābhimantrya astrādirakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tadbindubhis triśaḥ śirasi gurupādukām ārādhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated it seven times, he should sprinkle himself and the worship implements with drops of that water. With that water he should construct the previously described maṇḍala, combine the first vessel in the same way, place in it the first, next, and middle substances, worship the fire, sun, and moon kalās, consecrate them with the <s>Vakratuṇḍa</s> Gāyatrī and with the ṛc beginning 'gaṇānāṃ tvā,' perform the protection beginning with the weapon-mantra, and with drops from it worship the guru's sandals three times on his head.

children.text: purato raktacandananirmite pīṭhe mahāgaṇapatipratimāyāṃ vā caturasrāṣṭadalaṣaṭkoṇatrikoṇamaye cakre vā tīvrāyai jvālinyai nandāyai bhogadāyai kāmarūpiṇyai ugrāyai tejovatyai satyāyai vighnanāśinyai ṛṃ dharmāya ṝṃ jñānāya ﾱṃ vairāgyāya ﾲṃ aiśvaryāya ṛṃ adharmāya ṝṃ ajñānāya ﾱṃ avairāgyāya ﾲṃ anaiśvaryāya nama iti pīṭhaśaktīr dharmādyaṣṭakaṃ cābhyarcya mūlam uccārya mahāgaṇapatim āvāhayāmīty āvāhya pañcadhopacarya daśadhā saṃtarpya mūlena mithunāṅgabrāhmyādīndrādirūpapañcāvaraṇapūjāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In front, on a seat made of red sandalwood, or in an image of <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, or in a cakra composed of a square, eight-petaled lotus, hexagon, and triangle, he should worship the pīṭha powers: <s>Tīvrā</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Bhogadā</s>, <s>Kāmarūpiṇī</s>, <s>Ugrā</s>, <s>Tejovatī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Vighnanāśinī</s>; and the octad beginning with <s>dharma</s> (righteous order): 'ṛṃ, obeisance to <s>Dharma</s>; ṝṃ, to <s>Jñāna</s>; [corrupt bīja], to <s>Vairāgya</s>; [corrupt bīja], to <s>Aiśvarya</s>; ṛṃ, to <s>Adharma</s>; ṝṃ, to <s>Ajñāna</s>; [corrupt bīja], to <s>Avairāgya</s>; [corrupt bīja], to <s>Anaiśvarya</s>.' Having uttered the root mantra, he should invoke him with 'I invoke <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>,' honor him with the five services, satiate him ten times, and perform the worship of the five enclosures, in the forms of the paired limbs, <s>Brāhmī</s> and the others, and <s>Indra</s> and the others, with the root mantra.

children.text: trikoṇe devaḥ tasya ṣaḍasrasyāntarāle śrīśrīpatyādicaturmithunāni aṅgāni ca ṛddhyāmodādiṣaṇmithunāni ṣaḍasre mithunadvayaṃ ṣaḍasrobhayapārśvayos tatsandhiṣv aṅgāni brāhmyādyā aṣṭadale caturasrāṣṭadikṣv indrādyāḥ pūjyāḥ sarvatra devatānāmasu śrīpūrvaṃ pādukām uccārya pūjayāmīty aṣṭākṣarīṃ yojayet ||
children.translated_text: The deity is in the triangle. In the interval of its hexagon are the four pairs beginning with <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Śrīpati</s>, and the limb-deities. The six pairs beginning with <s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>Āmoda</s> are in the hexagon; a pair is on the two sides of the hexagon, and the limb-deities are at its junctions. <s>Brāhmī</s> and the others are in the eight-petaled lotus, and <s>Indra</s> and the others are to be worshiped in the eight directions of the square. Everywhere, before the names of the deities, he should add 'śrī,' utter 'pādukā,' and join the eight-syllabled phrase 'pūjayāmi.'

children.text: evaṃ pañcāvaraṇīm iṣṭvā punar devaṃ gaṇanāthaṃ daśadhopatarpya ṣoḍaśopacārair upacarya praṇavamāyānte sarvavighnakṛdbhyaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo huṃ svāhā iti triḥ paṭhitvā baliṃ dattvā gaṇapatibuddhyaikaṃ baṭukaṃ siddhalakṣmībuddhyaikāṃ śaktiṃ cāhūya gandhapuṣpākṣatair abhyarcyādimopādimamadhyamān dattvā mama nirvighnaṃ mantrasiddhir bhūyād ity anugrahaṃ kārayitvā namaskṛtya yathāśakti japet ||
children.translated_text: Having thus worshiped the five enclosures, he should again satiate the deity <s>Gaṇanātha</s> ten times, honor him with the sixteen services, recite three times, after praṇava and māyā, 'To all makers of obstacles, to all beings, huṃ svāhā,' and give the bali. Then he should summon one boy with the understanding that he is <s>Gaṇapati</s>, and one woman with the understanding that she is <s>Siddhalakṣmī</s>; worship them with sandal, flowers, and unhusked rice; give the first, next, and middle substances; have them grant the blessing, 'May my mantra-accomplishment be free from obstacles'; bow down; and recite the mantra according to his ability.

children.text: yady agnikāryasaṃpattiḥ baleḥ pūrvaṃ vidhivat saṃskṛte 'gnau svāhāntaiḥ śrīśrīpatyādivighnakartṛparyantaiḥ mantrair hutvā punar āgatya devaṃ trivāraṃ saṃtarpya yogyaiḥ saha mapañcakam urarīkṛtya mahāgaṇapatim ātmany udvāsya siddhasaṅkalpaḥ sukhī viharet iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: If the fire-rite is possible, before the bali, in a fire ritually consecrated according to rule, he should offer oblations with mantras ending in svāhā, beginning with <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Śrīpati</s> and ending with the remover of obstacles. Then, returning again, having satisfied the deity three times and having accepted the five m's together with suitable companions, he should dismiss <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s> into himself and, his resolve accomplished, live happily. Thus auspiciousness.

children.text: Chapter 3
evaṃ gaṇapatim iṣṭvā vidhūtasamastavighnavyatikaraḥ śakticakraikanāyikāyāḥ śrīlalitāyāḥ kramam ārabheta ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Gaṇapati</s> in this way, and having shaken off every conjunction of obstacles, he should begin the sequence of <s>Śrīlalitā</s>, the sole mistress of the circle of powers.

children.text: brāhme muhūrte brāhmaṇo muktasvāpaḥ pāpavilāpāya paramaśivarūpaṃ gurum abhimṛśya ||
children.translated_text: At the brāhma muhūrta, the brāhmaṇa, freed from sleep, should touch or recollect the guru, who has the form of supreme <s>Śiva</s>, for the dissolution of sin.

children.text: mūlādividhibilaparyantaṃ taḍitkoṭikaḍārāṃ taruṇadivākarapiñjarāṃ jvalantīṃ mūlasaṃvidaṃ dhyātvā tadraśminihatakaśmalajālaḥ kādiṃ hādiṃ vā mūlavidyāṃ manasā daśavāram āvartya ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated, from the root up to the aperture of Brahman, on the root consciousness, flashing with ten million lightning bolts, tawny like the young sun, and blazing, with the net of his impurities struck down by its rays, he should mentally repeat ten times the root vidyā, either beginning with ka or beginning with ha.

children.text: snānakarmaṇi prāpte mūlena dattvā triḥ salilāñjalīn tris tadabhimantritāḥ pītvāpas tris saṃtarpya triḥ prokṣyātmānaṃ paridhāya vāsasī hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ saḥ ity uktvā mārtāṇḍabhairavāya prakāśaśaktisahitāya svāheti tris savitre dattārghyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the act of bathing has come, he should offer three handfuls of water with the root mantra, drink water consecrated by it three times, satisfy the waters three times, sprinkle himself three times, put on two garments, say 'hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ saḥ,' and then offer arghya three times to <s>Savitṛ</s>, saying, 'svāhā to <s>Mārtāṇḍabhairava</s>, together with the power of manifestation.'

children.text: tanmaṇḍalamadhye navayonicakram anucintya vācam uccārya tripurasundari vidmahe kāmam uccārya pīṭhakāmini dhīmahi śaktim uccārya tan naḥ klinnā pracodayād iti trir maheśyai dattārghyaḥ śatam aṣṭottaram āmṛśya manuṃ maunam ālambya ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of that disk he should contemplate the nine-yoni cakra and, uttering 'speech,' 'may we know <s>Tripurasundarī</s>,' uttering 'desire,' 'may we meditate on the lover of the pīṭha,' uttering 'power,' 'may that moist one impel us'; he should offer arghya three times to <s>Maheśī</s>, touch or recite the mantra one hundred and eight times, and take up silence.

children.text: yāgamandiraṃ gatvā kﾱptākalpaḥ saṅkalpākalpo vā pīṭhamanunā āsane samupaviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to the sacrificial chamber, properly arranged, or arranged according to his resolve, he should sit on the seat with the pīṭha-mantra.

children.text: tritārīm uccārya raktadvādaśaśaktiyuktāya dīpanāthāya nama iti bhūmau muñcet puṣpāñjalim ||
children.translated_text: Uttering the three tārās, he should release onto the ground a handful of flowers, saying, 'Homage to <s>Dīpanātha</s>, endowed with the twelve red powers.'

children.text: sarveṣāṃ mantrāṇām ādau tritārīsaṃyogaḥ
children.translated_text: At the beginning of all mantras there is conjunction with the three tārās.

children.text: tritārī vāṅmāyākamalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The three tārās are speech, Māyā, and Kamalā.

children.text: purataḥ pañcaśakticatuḥśrīkaṇṭhamelanarūpaṃ bhūsadanatrayavalitrayabhūpapatradikpatrabhuvanāradruhiṇāravidhikoṇadikkoṇatrikoṇabinducakramayaṃ mahācakrarājaṃ sindūrakuṅkumalikhitaṃ cāmīkarakaladhautapañcaloharatnasphaṭikādyutkīrṇaṃ vā niveśya ||
children.translated_text: In front he should set down the great royal cakra, formed by the union of five powers and four Śrīkaṇṭhas, consisting of the three earth-abodes, the three enclosures, the earth-petals, the directional petals, the world-spokes, the Brahmā-spokes, the vidhi-corners, the directional corners, the triangle, and the bindu, drawn with vermilion and saffron, or engraved in gold, silver, the five metals, jewel, crystal, and the like.

children.text: tatra mahācakre amṛtāmbhonidhaye ratnadvīpāya nānāvṛkṣamahodyānāya kalpavṛkṣavāṭikāyai santānavāṭikāyai haricandanavāṭikāyai mandāravāṭikāyai pārijātavāṭikāyai kadambavāṭikāyai puṣparāgaratnaprākārāya padmarāgaratnaprākārāya gomedharatnaprākārāya vajraratnaprākārāya vaiḍūryaratnaprākārāya indranīlaratnaprākārāya muktāratnaprākārāya marakataratnaprākārāya vidrumaratnaprākārāya māṇikyamaṇḍapāya sahasrastambhamaṇḍapāya amṛtavāpikāyai ānandavāpikāyai vimarśavāpikāyai bālātapodgārāya candrikodgārāya mahāśṛṅgāraparighāyai mahāpadmāṭavyai cintāmaṇigṛharājāya pūrvāmnāyamayapūrvadvārāya dakṣiṇāmnāyamayadakṣiṇadvārāya paścimāmnāyamayapaścimadvārāyottarāmnāyamayottaradvārāya ratnapradīpavalayāya maṇimayamahāsiṃhāsanāya brahmamayaikamañcapādāya viṣṇumayaikamañcapādāya rudramayaikamañcapādāya īśvaramayaikamañcapādāya sadāśivamayaikamañcaphalakāya haṃsatūlatalpāya haṃsatūlamahopadhānāya kausumbhāstaraṇāya mahāvitānakāya mahājavanikāyai namaḥ iti catuścatvāriṃśanmantrais tattad akhilaṃ bhāvayitvā arcayitvā ||
children.translated_text: There, in that great cakra, with the forty-four mantras ending in 'namaḥ,' he should imagine and worship each entire element: the ocean of nectar, the jewel-island, the great garden of many trees, the grove of wish-granting trees, the grove of santāna trees, the grove of yellow sandalwood, the grove of mandāra trees, the grove of pārijāta trees, the grove of kadamba trees, the enclosure of topaz jewels, the enclosure of ruby jewels, the enclosure of gomedha jewels, the enclosure of diamond jewels, the enclosure of vaidūrya jewels, the enclosure of sapphire jewels, the enclosure of pearl jewels, the enclosure of emerald jewels, the enclosure of coral jewels, the ruby pavilion, the thousand-pillared pavilion, the well of nectar, the well of bliss, the well of reflective awareness, the outpouring of young sunlight, the outpouring of moonlight, the great enclosure of love, the great lotus forest, the royal house of wish-fulfilling gems, the eastern door made of the eastern transmission, the southern door made of the southern transmission, the western door made of the western transmission, the northern door made of the northern transmission, the circle of jewel lamps, the great jewel lion-throne, the one couch-leg made of <s>Brahmā</s>, the one couch-leg made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the one couch-leg made of <s>Rudra</s>, the one couch-leg made of <s>Īśvara</s>, the couch-board made of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the swan-down bed, the great swan-down pillow, the safflower-colored covering, the great canopy, and the great curtain.

children.text: gandhapuṣpākṣatādīṃś ca dakṣiṇabhāge dīpān abhito dattvā mūlena cakram abhyarcya mūlatrikhaṇḍaiḥ prathamatryasre ||
children.translated_text: Having placed perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, and the like on the southern side, and lamps on both sides, he should worship the cakra with the root mantra and the first triangle with the three sections of the root mantra.

children.text: vāyvagnisalilavarṇayukprāṇāyāmaiḥ śoṣaṇaṃ saṃdahanam āplāvanaṃ ca vidhāya ||
children.translated_text: With prāṇāyāmas joined to the syllables of wind, fire, and water, he should perform drying, burning, and flooding.

children.text: triḥ prāṇān āyamya ||
children.translated_text: He should restrain the breaths three times.

children.text: apasarpantu te bhūtā ye bhūtā bhuvi saṃsthitāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let those beings withdraw, the beings who are established on the earth;

children.text: ye bhūtā vighnakartāras te naśyantu śivājñayā
children.translated_text: those beings who make obstacles, let them perish by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: iti vāmapādapārṣṇighātakarāsphoṭasamudañcitavaktras tālatrayaṃ dattvā devyahambhāvayuktaḥ svaśarīre vajrakavacanyāsajālaṃ vidadhīta ||
children.translated_text: Saying this, with his face raised after striking the heel of the left foot and snapping the fingers, and after giving three claps, united with the state 'I am the goddess,' he should perform on his own body the network of nyāsas of the adamantine armor.

children.text: binduyukśrīkaṇṭhānantatārtīyaiḥ madhyamāditalaparyantaṃ kṛtakaraśuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the tārās of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and <s>Ananta</s> joined with the bindu, he has purified his hands from the middle finger down to the palms.

children.text: kumārīm uccārya mahātripurasundarīpadam ātmānaṃ rakṣa rakṣeti hṛdaye añjaliṃ dattvā ||
children.translated_text: Uttering <s>Kumārī</s> and the word <s>Mahātripurasundarī</s>, he should place his joined palms at his heart, saying, 'Protect me, protect me.'

children.text: māyākāmaśaktīr uccārya devyātmāsanāya namaḥ iti svasyāsanaṃ dattvā ||
children.translated_text: Uttering Māyā, Kāma, and Śakti, he should provide his own seat, saying, 'Homage to the seat of the self as goddess.'

children.text: śivayugbālām uccārya śrīcakrāsanāya namaḥ śivabhṛguyugbālām uccārya sarvamantrāsanāya namo bhuvanāmadanau blem uccārya sādhyasiddhāsanāya namaḥ iti cakramantradevatāsanaṃ tribhir mantraiś cakre kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Uttering Śiva-yug-Bālā, he should say, 'Homage to the seat of the Śrīcakra'; uttering Śiva-Bhṛgu-yug-Bālā, 'Homage to the seat of all mantras'; uttering Bhuvanā and Madana and 'blem,' 'Homage to the seat of the sādhya and siddha.' Thus with three mantras he should make the seat of the cakra, mantras, and deities in the cakra.

children.text: bālādvirāvṛttyā tridvyekadaśatridvisaṅkhyāṅgulivinyāsaiḥ kﾱptaṣaḍaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made the six limbs, by twice repeating from bālā, with placements of the fingers counted as three, two, one, ten, three, and two aṅgulas.

children.text: sabindūn aco blūm uccārya vaśinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti śirasi
children.translated_text: Having uttered the vowels with bindu as blūm, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Vaśinī Vāgdevatā</s>,’ on the head.

children.text: sarvatra vargāṇāṃ binduyogaḥ
children.translated_text: Everywhere there is conjunction with bindu for the groups of letters.

children.text: kavargaṃ kalahrīṃ ca nigadya kāmeśvarīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti lalāṭe
children.translated_text: Having recited the ka-class together with kalahrīṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Kāmeśvarī Vāgdevatā</s>,’ on the forehead.

children.text: cuṃ gaditvā nvlīṃ modinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti bhrūmadhye
children.translated_text: Having said cuṃ and nvlīṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Modinī Vāgdevatā</s>,’ between the eyebrows.

children.text: ṭuṃ bhaṇitvā ylūṃ vimalāvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti kaṇṭhe
children.translated_text: Having pronounced ṭuṃ and ylūṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Vimalā Vāgdevatā</s>,’ on the throat.

children.text: tuṃ ca procya jmrīṃ aruṇāvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti hṛdi
children.translated_text: Having uttered tuṃ and jmrīṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Aruṇā Vāgdevatā</s>,’ on the heart.

children.text: puṃ ca hslvyūṃ uccārya jayinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti nābhau
children.translated_text: Having uttered puṃ and hslvyūṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Jayinī Vāgdevatā</s>,’ on the navel.

children.text: yādicatuṣkaṃ jhmryūṃ uccārya sarveśvarīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti liṅge
children.translated_text: Having uttered the four beginning with ya and jhmryūṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Sarveśvarī Vāgdevatā</s>,’ on the liṅga.

children.text: śādiṣaṭkaṃ kṣmrīṃ ākhyāya kaulinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ iti mūle ||
children.translated_text: Having declared the six beginning with śa and kṣmrīṃ, one says, ‘Obeisance to <s>Kaulinī Vāgdevatā</s>,’ at the root.

children.text: mūlavidyāpañcadaśavarṇān mūrdhni mūle hṛdi cakṣustritaye śrutidvayamukhabhujayugalapṛṣṭhajānuyugalanābhiṣu vinyasya ṣoḍhā cakre nyasyānyasya vā ||
children.translated_text: He should place the fifteen syllables of the root vidyā on the head, at the root, on the heart, on the three eyes, on the two ears, the mouth, the pair of arms, the back, the pair of knees, and the navel; he should place them sixfold in the cakra, or otherwise.

children.text: śuddhāmbhasā vāmabhāge trikoṇaṣaṭkoṇavṛttacaturaśramaṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā puṣpair abhyarcya sādhāraṃ śaṅkhaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya śuddhajalam āpūrya ādimabinduṃ dattvā ṣaḍaṅgenābhyarcya vidyayā abhimantrya tajjalavipruḍbhiḥ ātmānaṃ pūjopakaraṇāni ca saṃprokṣya ||
children.translated_text: With pure water, on the left side, he should make a maṇḍala of triangle, hexagon, circle, and square; worship it with flowers; establish a common conch; fill it with pure water; add the initial bindu; worship it with the six limbs; consecrate it with the vidyā; and sprinkle himself and the implements of worship with drops of that water.

children.text: tajjalena trikoṇaṣaṭkoṇavṛttacaturasramaṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā madhyaṃ vidyayā vidyākhaṇḍais trikoṇaṃ bījāvṛttyā ṣaḍaśraṃ sampūjya vācam uccārya agnimaṇḍalāya daśakalātmane arghyapātrādhārāya namaḥ iti pratiṣṭhāpya ādhāraṃ prapūjya pāvakīḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With that water he should make a maṇḍala of triangle, hexagon, circle, and square; worship the center with the vidyā, the triangle with the sections of the vidyā, and the hexagon by repetition of the seed; then, uttering the vāc, he should establish the support with ‘Obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala, consisting of ten kalās, the support of the arghya vessel,’ worship the support, and worship the fiery kalās.

children.text: madanād upari sūryamaṇḍalāya dvādaśakalātmane arghyapātrāya namaḥ iti saṃvidhāya pātraṃ saṃspṛśya kalāḥ saurīḥ sauḥ somamaṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśakalātmane arghyāmṛtāya namaḥ iti pūrayitvā ādimaṃ dattvopādimamadhyamau pūjayitvā vidhoḥ kalāṣoḍaśakam ||
children.translated_text: Above Madana he should arrange the vessel with ‘Obeisance to the solar maṇḍala, consisting of twelve kalās, the arghya vessel’; touching the vessel, he should worship the solar kalās; with ‘sauḥ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala, consisting of sixteen kalās, the nectar of arghya,’ he should fill it, add the first, worship the subordinate first and middle, and then worship the sixteen kalās of the moon.

children.text: tatra vilikhya tryasram akathādimayarekhaṃ halakṣayugāntasthitahaṃsabhāsvaraṃ vākkāmaśaktiyuktakoṇaṃ haṃsenārādhya bahir vṛttaṣaṭkoṇaṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍasraṃ ṣaḍaṅgena purobhāgādy abhyarcya mūlena saptadhā abhimantrya dattagandhākṣatapuṣpadhūpadīpaḥ tadvipruḍbhiḥ prokṣitapūjādravyaḥ sarvaṃ vidyāmayaṃ kṛtvā tat spṛṣṭvā caturnavatimantrān japet ||
children.translated_text: There he should draw a triangle whose lines consist of the series beginning with a, ka, and tha, shining with haṃsa placed between the two ending consonants ha and kṣa, its corners furnished with vāc, kāma, and śakti; he should worship it with haṃsa, make outside it a circle and hexagon, worship the hexagon from the front onward with the six limbs, consecrate it seven times with the root mantra, offer sandal, rice, flowers, incense, and lamp, sprinkle the worship materials with its drops, make everything consist of the vidyā, touch it, and recite ninety-four mantras.

children.text: tritārīnamassaṃpuṭitāḥ tejastritayakalā aṣṭatriṃśat
children.translated_text: The thirty-eight kalās of the three lights are enclosed by the three tārās and namas.

children.text: sṛṣṭiṛddhismṛtimedhākāntilakṣmīdyutisthirāsthitisiddhayo brahmakalā daśa
children.translated_text: Creation, prosperity, memory, intelligence, beauty, fortune, radiance, firmness, stability, and accomplishment are the ten kalās of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: jarā pālinī śāntir īśvarī ratikāmike varadāhlādinī prītir dīrghā viṣṇukalā daśa
children.translated_text: Old age, Pālinī, peace, sovereignty, Rati, Kāmikā, boon-giving, delighting, affection, and length are the ten kalās of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇā raudrī bhayā nidrā tandrī kṣudhā krodhinī kriyodgārīmṛtyavo rudrakalā daśa
children.translated_text: Sharpness, Raudrī, fear, sleep, drowsiness, hunger, anger, action, vomiting, and death are the ten kalās of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: pītā śvetāruṇāsitāś catasra īśvarakalāḥ
children.translated_text: Yellow, white, red, and black are the four kalās of <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: nivṛttipratiṣṭhāvidyāśāntīndhikādīpikārecikāmocikāparāsūkṣmāsūkṣmāmṛtājñānājñānāmṛtāpyāyinīvyāpinīvyomarūpāḥ ṣoḍaśa sadāśivakalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Vidyā, Śānti, Indhikā, Dīpikā, Recikā, Mocikā, Parā, Sūkṣmā, Sūkṣmāmṛtā, Jñānā, Jñānāmṛtā, Āpyāyinī, Vyāpinī, and Vyomarūpā are the sixteen kalās of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: haṃsaś śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasaddhotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat
children.translated_text: The haṃsa dwelling in purity, the Vasu dwelling in the midspace, the hotṛ dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house,

children.text: nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vayomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ||
children.translated_text: dwelling among men, dwelling among the excellent, dwelling in truth, dwelling in the sky, born from the waters, born from cows, born from truth, born from the mountain: the great truth.

children.text: pra tadviṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Viṣṇu</s> is praised for his heroic power, like a fearsome beast roaming in difficult places, dwelling on the mountain heights,

children.text: yasyoruṣu triṣu vikrameṣv adhikṣiyanti bhuvanāni vviśvā ||
children.translated_text: in whose three wide strides all the worlds dwell.

children.text: tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam
children.translated_text: We worship the three-eyed one, fragrant and increasing nourishment;

children.text: urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt ||
children.translated_text: as from its stem a cucumber, may I be released from death, not from immortality.

children.text: tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise always behold that supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: divīva cakṣur ātatam ||
children.translated_text: spread out like an eye in heaven.

children.text: tadviprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ samindhate
children.translated_text: The inspired and wakeful sages kindle

children.text: viṣṇor yat paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: that supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu
children.translated_text: May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb; may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fashion the forms;

children.text: āsiñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Prajāpati</s> pour it in; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo in you.

children.text: garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi sarasvati
children.translated_text: Place the embryo, <s>Sinīvālī</s>; place the embryo, <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāv ādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
children.translated_text: may the two divine <s>Aśvins</s>, garlanded with lotuses, set the embryo in you.

children.text: ity ete pañcamantrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are the five mantras.

children.text: mūlavidyā cāhatya caturnavatimantrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with the root vidyā, there are in all ninety-four mantras.

children.text: atha haike pañcabhir akhaṇḍādyair abhimantraṇam āmananti ||
children.translated_text: Now some teach consecration by means of the five mantras beginning with akhaṇḍa.

children.text: akhaṇḍaikarasānandakare parasudhātmani
children.translated_text: O you who produce the bliss of undivided single essence, O supreme nectar-self,

children.text: svacchandasphuraṇam atra nidhehy akulanāyike ||
children.translated_text: place here spontaneous manifestation, O mistress of the akula.

children.text: akulasthāmṛtākāre śuddhajñānakare pare
children.translated_text: O supreme one, whose form is the nectar abiding in the akula, who produces pure knowledge,

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ nidhehy asmin vastuni klinnarūpiṇi ||
children.translated_text: place immortality in this substance, O one whose form is moistened.

children.text: tadrūpiṇy aikarasyatvaṃ kṛtvā hy etat svarūpiṇi
children.translated_text: O you of that form, O own-form, having made this into a state of single essence,

children.text: bhūtvā parāmṛtākārā mayi citsphuraṇaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: become of the form of supreme nectar and produce the manifestation of consciousness in me.

children.text: iti tisro 'nuṣṭubho vidyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus there are three anuṣṭubh vidyās.

children.text: atho vācaṃ blūṃ jhraum iti jūṃ saḥ iti coktvā amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya svāheti caturtho mantraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, having uttered vāc, blūṃ, jhraum, then jūṃ saḥ, he says: ‘O nectar, born of nectar, mistress of nectar, showerer of nectar, cause nectar to flow, cause it to flow, svāhā’; this is the fourth mantra.

children.text: vāgbhavo vada vada tato vāgvādini vāṅmadanaklinne kledini kledaya mahākṣobhaṃ kuruyugalaṃ mādanaṃ śaktir mokṣaṃ kuru kuru śabdo hasacaturdaśapañcadaśapiṇḍaḥ sahacaturdaśaṣoḍaśapiṇḍaś ceti pañcamīyaṃ vidyaitābhiḥ abhimantrya jyotirmayaṃ tad arghyaṃ vidhāya ||
children.translated_text: The seed-syllable of speech: 'Speak, speak.' Then, 'O <s>Vāgvādinī</s>, moistened by the passion of speech, O <s>Kledinī</s>, cause to be moistened; produce great agitation; the pair "kuru", the erotic syllable, the śakti, the liberating syllable; "kuru kuru"'; the word is a mass of the fourteenth and fifteenth with 'hasa', and also a mass of the fourteenth and sixteenth with 'saha'. This is the fifth vidyā. Having consecrated with these, he should make that arghya luminous.

children.text: tadbindubhis triśaḥ śirasi gurupādukām iṣṭvā ārdraṃ jvalati jyotir aham asmi jyotir jvalati brahmāham asmi yo 'ham asmi brahmāham asmi aham asmi brahmāham asmi aham evāhaṃ māṃ juhomi svāheti tad bindum ātmanaḥ kuṇḍalinyāṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: With drops of it, three times upon the head, having worshipped the guru's sandals, he should say: 'Moist, a light blazes; I am the light; the light blazes. I am <s>brahman</s>. What I am, I am <s>brahman</s>. I am, I am <s>brahman</s>. I myself am I; I offer myself into myself. Svāhā.' Thus he should offer that drop into his own <s>kuṇḍalinī</s>.

children.text: etad arghyaśodhanam iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: This is the purification of the arghya. Thus auspiciousness.
